Ravi (capacity): Heads-up — Black Friday planning kickoff. I sketched a regional tranche approach: staggered warm pools + on-demand spill lanes. Want quick sanity check on GPU-hour hit and network limits.
Ava (infra): Sounds sensible. Can you share the tranche sizes? e.g., % of baseline to prewarm per region?
Ravi (capacity): Proposed: NA-west 35%, EU-central 25%, APAC 20%, spill/reserve 20%. These are percent of projected peak qps. Rough sim -> ~96k GPU-hours over 72h for prewarm + burst. :thinking_face:
Devon (sre): 96k seems plausible but we need to account for region egress and cross-zone networking. EU inter-region routing has 10% higher tail latency under load last time.
Lina (prod): Product wants <150ms p95 for interactive flows. If EU has higher tail, can we route EU interactive to NA fallback? That might violate data locality for some customers.
Ava (infra): We can set policy: interactive_latency_sensitive -> route pref to local, fallback to NA-west only if local queue > 80% capacity. Non-sensitive -> use cheapest lane (quantized endpoints).
Ravi (capacity): Also proposing phased warm pools: phase 1 small warm (50% of tranche) 12h prewarm, phase 2 full warm 2h before window. Reduces idle hours but still gives KV cache warm. Any objections?
Devon (sre): Phased warm looks good. Need playbook for quick rollback of warm pools if we see bad perf. Suggest prebuilt rollback job:
```
# rollback warm pool to baseline
redwoodctl cluster scale --pool bf-warm --replicas 0 --region eu-central
```
Ava (infra): I'll add that job to ops-runbook. Also we should tag prewarm instances with costcenter=bf2026 so billing filters are easy.
ops-bot: reminder — quota check: eu-central GPUs available: 420; na-west GPUs available: 720; apac GPUs available: 190. (Runbook: /ops/quota)
Ravi (capacity): Those numbers mean we need to split tranche into micro-lanes. If eu-central only has 420 GPUs, we should not prewarm more than ~340 there to leave headroom for on-demand.
Lina (prod): What about model variants? Can we route to a smaller quantized variant during peak to reduce GPU-hours? Product is ok if quality delta is small for non-pay customers.
Ava (infra): Yes — we have v2-8q variant tested. Latency is ~10% faster and cost ~30% lower. We can set rollout rules: default -> full model; overflow -> 8q. Will need to ensure eval team signs off on quality gates.
Devon (sre): Network note: APAC region has occasional midnight maintenance windows. Schedule prewarm to avoid 00:00-02:00 local. Also set health-check window to tighter p95 detection during BF window.
Ravi (capacity): I'll run an updated sim with the phased warm + quantized overflow and post results by EOD. Quick ask: whoever owns the EU network throttles, can we get an emergency contact and a static route for fallback? @Ava
Ava (infra): On it. Adding contact + static route to runbook. Also adding a cheap synthetic that hits the warm pool every 30s to keep KV hot.
Lina (prod): Adding a feature flag to toggle quantized overflow per customer tier. Ops can flip if quality complaints spike.
Devon (sre): One more: add a circuit-breaker so if p99 > 500ms for 5m, automatically divert 25% traffic to secondary region.
Ravi (capacity): Great. I'll include cost delta table in the sim: baseline vs phased-warm vs phased-warm+8q. Expect to shave ~22% GPU-hours vs full warm.
Ava (infra): FYI I'll lock in prewarm instance types tomorrow after checking spot availability.
Ravi (capacity): Thanks team. I'll post sim output and a short ops checklist here when ready. :rocket:
ops-bot: ticket created — BF-2026-REGIONAL-TRANCHE (ops runbook link: /tickets/BF-2026-REGIONAL-TRANCHE)
